model_annotations.Bulgarian: This multi-level pie chart, or sunburst chart, illustrates the hierarchical categorization of different character types. The chart consists of a total of 16 distinct segments arranged across an inner and an outer ring. The inner ring displays three primary categories: "Virtual Characters" in light blue, which occupies the clear majority of the chart at approximately 60%; "Real Characters" in bright green, making up roughly 25%; and "Custom Characters" in pink, accounting for the remaining 15%. The outer ring further subdivides these primary categories into 13 smaller slices, colored in lighter pastel shades corresponding to their parent category's color. The light blue "Virtual Characters" section is divided into five outer slices labeled "Comic Characters" (which is visually the largest of this group), "Movie Characters," "Teleplay Characters," "Novel Characters," and "Game Characters." The pink "Custom Characters" section corresponds to a single, unlabeled outer slice. The light green "Real Characters" section is split into seven outer slices labeled "Scientists," "Artists," "Athletes," "Writers," "Musicians," "Actors," and "Influencers." The chart does not include a separate legend or numerical percentage labels; instead, category titles are placed directly within or adjacent to their respective segments. The text labels for the outer ring are color-coded to match their respective sections, utilizing dark blue text for virtual characters and dark green text for real characters. All slices are separated by thin white borders, and no segments are visually exploded or offset.
model_annotations.English: This image displays a two-level pie chart, also known as a sunburst chart, representing the composition of different character types. The chart is structured with an inner ring displaying three main categories and an outer ring containing thirteen corresponding subcategory slices. The inner ring consists of "Virtual Characters" in solid blue, which occupies the largest proportion at roughly two-thirds of the chart; "Real Characters" in solid green, taking up approximately one-fifth; and "Custom Characters" in solid pink, representing the smallest share. The outer ring expands on these main categories using lighter shades of the corresponding colors. The light blue section for "Virtual Characters" is divided into five slices labeled "Comic Characters" (which is visually the largest of this group), "Movie Characters", "Teleplay Characters", "Novel Characters", and "Game Characters". The light pink section for "Custom Characters" consists of a single, unlabeled slice. The light green section for "Real Characters" is divided into seven slices labeled "Scientists", "Artists", "Athletes", "Writers", "Musicians", "Actors", and "Influencers". The chart does not include a separate legend or explicit numerical percentage labels, relying instead on text labels placed directly on or adjacent to the slices. The outer text labels are color-coded in dark blue and dark green to match their respective sections, while the inner category labels are black. All slices are separated by thin white borders, with no segments visually exploded or offset, and the outer subcategories do not appear to be strictly ordered by size.
